To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a video based online intervention can be delivered to HIV positive gay, bisexual, and MSM and may lead to reductions serodiscordance CAS and increased disclosure.
an eHealth intervention delivered through multiple online mediums to a large, diverse sample of HIV positive GBSM may lead to reductions HIV transmission and increased HIV disclosure.
an online video based HIV prevention intervention was effective in reducing HIV transmission risk behaviors and improving social cognitions among HIV positive gay and bisexual men.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a new intervention to reduce HIV transmission risk among HIV positive GB MSM.
the development and evaluation of an online, video-based HIV risk reduction intervention for HIV-positive gay, bisexual, and MSM.
developing and evaluating an online, video-based, theory-driven intervention for HIV positive GBMSMs who struggle with ART and are at high risk for transmitting HIV to their partners.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the study protocol described the underlying theoretical framework, design, recruitment challenges and antifraud measure for a online video based randomized controlled trail that has the potential of decreasing HIV transmission risk behaviors.

the protocol for the Sex Positive! study was designed to evaluate a novel video based intervention to increase HIV disclosure and decrease transmission risk behaviors among a high risk population of HIV positive men who have sex without a condom with men.
this study will be a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the efficacy of the Sex Positive! intervention in reducing serodiscordance CAS and increasing HIV disclosure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are developing and testing an intervention to reduce HIV transmission among HIV positive gay, bisexual, and MSM who struggle with ART (antiretroviral) adherence.
we are developing an intervention to reduce HIV transmission among HIV positive gay and bisexual men.

the study protocol describes the theoretical framework, measures, study design (including the recruitment and fraud prevention measures), and challenges of an online, video-based randomized controlled trial with the potential to decrease the risk of HIV transmission in HIV-positive gay, bisexual, and men who have sex men who have difficulty adhering to antiretrovival therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intervention was feasible to develop and implement.
online interventions are feasible and acceptable among HIV positive GBSM.
we are developing an online, video-based intervention for HIV+ gay, bisexual and other men who use the internet to meet sex partners.
